O.outcome_detail: Agreement between automated and human total scores

cells.quote: To assess the credibility of its feedback, a pilot validation comparing automated scores with human ratings on 40 recordings was conducted (Section 3.5).
cells.note: The reported correlation results and mean scores are in the wiki entry but not in the supplied study-text excerpt; the quote therefore shows only the study's description of the pilot validation.

cells.quote: "Logical coherence ( r = 0.79, p < 0.001, 95% CI [0.64, 0.89]) and linguistic accuracy ( r = 0.63, p < 0.001, 95% CI [0.39, 0.78]) showed strong correlations with human ratings; delivery fluency (r = 0.45, p = 0.004, 95% CI [0.16, 0.67]) a moderate one; and information fidelity ( r = 0.12, p = 0.478, 95% CI [ −0.20, 0.41]) a weak, non-significant correlation."
cells.note: The dimension-level result is reported in the wiki entry; the supplied study-text excerpt mentions the pilot validation but does not include these statistics.

cells.quote: Logistic multivariate regression showed that female (OR = 0.73, 95% CI: 0.60–0.89, p = 0.002) and senior (OR = 0.48, 95% CI: 0.39–0.59, p < 0.001) students, and those who where involved in post-disaster reconstruction (OR = 0.68, 95% CI: 0.54–0.85, p = 0.001), were less likely to have school maladaptation, while those who were buried under a collapsed building (OR = 1.47, 95% CI: 1.04–2.09, p = 0.03) and suffered bereavement (OR = 1.77, 95% CI: 1.27–2.45, p = 0.001) had a higher risk of poor school adaptation.
cells.note: The study reports an association, not a manipulated treatment effect.

O.outcome_detail: Probable PTSD based on PTSD Checklist score ≥44

cells.quote: Multivariate logistic regression suggested that participants who experienced bereavement (OR = 1.60, 95% CI: 1.12–2.28 p = 0.009) were more likely to report PTSD (Table 5).
cells.note: Measured five years after the Yushu earthquake in a school-based survey; this is an association, not a causal treatment effect.
